description: 68 router cases over the root, pstack and named third-party skills (run with --include-pstack and --catalog-extra). Drafted 2026-11-27 by the main session and labelled blind by a fresh-context labeller that saw only prompts and the catalog; expected is the union of both label sets. Not owner-labelled.

cases.prompt: Review the changes on this branch since main before I open the PR.
cases.notes: Labeller (medium): code-review matches 'review since main' exactly; autoreview also fits as an explicitly requested review of a Git target.

cases.prompt: Check whether this branch follows our documented coding standards and actually does what issue #42 asked for.
Get a different model to review commit a1b2c3d; I don't want the model that wrote it grading it.
cases.notes: Labeller (medium): An independent single-model review points to autoreview; council also covers second-opinion change review across agent CLIs.

cases.prompt: Challenge this code hard and find the blind spots before we merge.
Run a thermo-nuclear review on this branch.
Here's my plan for moving billing to the new provider. Tear it apart: alternatives, evidence, trade-offs.
cases.notes: Labeller (medium): 'Alternatives, evidence, trade-offs' on a plan matches expert-review; 'tear it apart' is also an interrogate trigger for designs.

cases.prompt: Have three different agent CLIs deliberate on whether we should split this service, two rounds at most.
This module is a 3,000-line file full of nested conditionals. Give me the harshest maintainability review you can.
We deploy to production tomorrow. Give me the pre-deploy security verdict on this commit.
Do a full, deep security audit of this whole codebase with machine-readable findings.
Fix the IDOR in the invoices endpoint we found yesterday. You're authorized to change the code.
cases.notes: Labeller (medium): mneves-security covers authorized security fixes; tdd also fits because this is a bug fix.

cases.prompt: Before launch: do we have backups, rollback, billing safety, and someone on call?
Check the security of this branch's changes only, not the whole repository.
cases.notes: Labeller (medium): thermo-nuclear-review matches a branch-diff security scope but runs only when named; security-audit covers the whole codebase.

cases.prompt: Check the trust boundaries and privacy controls for the new user-upload feature.
Pen test this repository's source end to end.
Write me a prompt I can paste into another agent so it can continue this work.
I was away for an hour. What happened in this chat and what's waiting on me?
I lost my session yesterday. Rebuild what I was working on from my history.
Ana started PR #318 and went on leave. Finish it, but keep her credit.
Summarize what I committed over the last two weeks for my standup.
Say what you just told me again in plain words, no jargon.
Watch PR #77 until CI finishes and tell me if anyone requests changes.
CI is red on my PR. Find the failing check and fix it.
What did reviewers say on the current PR? Just summarize the comments.
This PR is six weeks old. Rebase it onto main and tell me if it should still exist.
Clean up my PR's commit history and description so it's easier to review.
git merge left conflicts in three files. Resolve them and make sure the tests still pass.
Post a reply on the GitHub PR thread explaining why we kept the retry loop.
Drive PR #12 to mergeable: fix failing CI and handle the simple review comments as they come in.
cases.notes: Labeller (medium): babysit-pr is a near-duplicate, but its description covers monitoring only, not fixing CI or comments.

cases.prompt: Before writing any code, sketch the types and module boundaries for the new sync engine.
We need to move 40 services from REST to gRPC this quarter. Design a plan someone can audit after stepping away.
Make this task deeper, not bigger, and rewrite my prompt.
Grill me on this plan until it holds up.
Before you start, tell me in your own words what you think I'm trying to achieve.
Survey this repo and give me prioritized improvement plans another agent can implement. Don't change any code.
The payments and notifications modules are tangled together. Plan a behavior-preserving refactor of just that area.
How ready is this repo for AI agents to work in? What friction will they hit?
Let's settle the terminology for this codebase and write it down in a glossary.
Split this implementation across agents, send the backend part to Codex, and review what comes back.
Fan out 8 workers to check every endpoint for missing auth, then give me one report.
Have four agents each attempt the parser rewrite, then merge the best parts of each.
This is a multi-day implementation. Set it up so the work keeps going across many rounds.
cases.notes: Labeller (medium): Orchestrator covers long-running implementation; figure-it-out is a weaker fit because a narrower skill applies.

cases.prompt: Keep a decision log for this unattended overnight run so I can audit it in the morning.
The export endpoint started throwing 500s after yesterday's deploy. Diagnose it.
Why does the cache use a 37-second TTL? Who picked that, and based on what?
How does request authentication flow through this codebase, file by file?
Before I ship this config change, what else could it break outside the diff?
I measured a 30% speedup on the new index. Vet that number before I tell the team.
Search got 3x slower this week. Find out what regressed.
Fix the off-by-one in pagination, and write the failing test first.
Our suite has a lot of tests that check nothing real. Trim them, with evidence for each one.
Prove the migration actually worked. I want an independent verdict, not a review.
Generate a project-local skill that drives our app the way a user does, to verify features.
Agents keep making the same mistake with our date handling. Make it impossible to repeat.
Ship it.
cases.notes: Plain ship authorizes no deploy and is not /full-stop. Labeller (medium): Plain 'ship' explicitly does not invoke mneves-ship-deploy, and no other catalog skill covers a bare ship request.

cases.prompt: That's the plan. Full stop.
Take this change all the way to a ready PR without stopping to ask me.
cases.notes: full-stop needs its name. Labeller (medium): full-stop fits the intent but runs only when invoked by name; show-me-your-work is a weak alternative for unattended runs.

cases.prompt: What's the expert term for a thing that holds settings? Teach me the vocabulary.
cases.notes: reframe runs only when invoked by name. Labeller (medium): reframe matches the intent but runs only by name; teach and domain-modeling target codebase work, not a general vocabulary question.

cases.prompt: Give this branch a harsh review for bugs.
cases.notes: thermo reviews need their name. Labeller (medium): Thermo reviews require naming, and the code-quality one is about maintainability, not bugs; autoreview or adversarial interrogate fit.

cases.prompt: Rename the variable `tmp` to `retryCount` in utils.ts.
Fix the typo in the README heading.
What's the difference between a mutex and a semaphore?
Add a `--verbose` flag to the CLI that prints each step.
cases.notes: Labeller (medium): Small feature; tdd's description covers any feature change, but skipping a skill is also reasonable.

cases.prompt: Implementation's done and tests pass. Now independently confirm it works before I call it finished.
It's ready. Deploy it to production now; this is my project.
The plan is approved. Before we build, red-team its riskiest assumption.
cases.notes: Labeller (medium): Stress-testing a decision fits expert-review; interrogate also covers adversarial attacks on a design.

cases.prompt: The feature is built. Now write the PR description.
cases.notes: Labeller (medium): technical-writing explicitly covers PR descriptions; make-pr-easy-to-review is for improving an existing PR.

cases.prompt: We're about to deploy to staging. Check operational readiness first.
